title: Merge Overlapping Subintervals
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
intuition: Sorting by start time means any interval can only overlap the one currently open. That reduces merging to a single comparison per interval.

approaches.title: Optimal: sort then extend or push
approaches.idea: If the next start <= current end, extend the end; else start a new interval.
approaches.whyWorks: After sorting by start, an interval that does not overlap the open one cannot overlap any earlier one.

edgeCases: Touching intervals [1,2],[2,3] — merge or not? Clarify
commonMistakes: Setting end = next_end instead of max(end, next_end), which loses nested intervals
patternRecognition: Interval problems: sort by start to merge, sort by end to schedule greedily
followUps: Insert an interval into a sorted list (#272)
interviewInsight: The max() on the end is the classic silent bug — a nested [1,10] inside gets truncated without it.
